newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end moderately higher, off peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end moderately higher, off peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended moderately higher but well below session peaks.
Brokers said afternoon turnover was generally light, with some long liquidation seen during the final half hour in front of more inflation figures and as the dollar lost ground to the yen.
The dollar fell on widespread rumors that a Washington-based consulting firm issued a statement saying the United States would support a stronger yen.
"We eased on the dollar's weakness," said one floor broker in U.S. Treasury bond futures.
"That (dollar fall) did bring selling into our market, but I think it was more or less knee-jerk selling," he added.
Futures had seen good two-way flows, with talk of large dealer buying and selling, plus rumors that a hedge fund early sold a large amount of bonds.

Some brokers also tied sales to corporate supply. Sources said Norfolk Southern Corp Wednesday issued some $4.3 billion in debt via an eight-part offering. They called the investment grade offering the largest in corporate bond history.
Players also evened up for Thursday's April U.S. consumer price index, seen up 0.1 percent with the core up 0.2 percent.
Futures rose early when the April producer price index fell 0.6 percent and the core rate dipped 0.1 percent. Economists expected flat PPI and a 0.1 percent core rate rise.

Some noted surprise that futures did not rise more on the PPI report, with even charts suggesting an upside bias. But they blamed the hesitancy on trepidation over whether benign inflation figures at this point still would deter the Federal Reserve from tigthening credit May 20.
June T-bonds rose 11/32 to 110-05/32, notes rose 7/32 to 107-12/32, munis rose 15/32 to 116-02/32, June bills rose 0.015 to 94.740, and December Eurodollars rose 0.030 to 93.700.
